summary: Frontend-only visual verification of the Discover screen category-chip icon swap (outline -> filled variants). Logged in as demo consumer (demo@consumer.com/password123), cycled through all 7 categories (All/Music/Art/Tech/Food/Sports/Other) in BOTH dark (default) and light themes. Bug FIXED: no white/light square-box artifact is visible inside ANY category chip icon in either theme — every active chip renders a solid, opaque glyph with a colored border + accent halo. The previously-transparent interior negative space (empty note-heads on musical-notes-outline, transparent die on hardware-chip-outline, empty thumb-hole on color-palette-outline, etc.) is gone because all seven icons now use the filled Ionicons variant (sparkles / musical-notes / color-palette / laptop / fast-food / trophy / apps). Regression checks all pass: chip spring scale + wiggle animation still plays on selection, chip label recolors to accent when active, header LinearGradient wash re-tints dynamically per category (pink/purple/orange/cyan/red/teal/slate), poster shelves (Featured / Free & popular / Happening tonight / More near you) render with FREE badge, tab bar (Discover / My Tickets / Profile) navigates correctly, and Profile Dark-theme switch flips the whole app light<->dark instantly. No React Native red screen. Note: Deprecated shadow* props and pointerEvents prop warnings persist (carry-over from iteration_4, not related to this fix).

react_native_issues.issue: Console warns '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow".' on app boot (fired twice). Same warning reported in iteration_4. Originates from shadows.card in /app/frontend/src/theme.ts, applied via ...shadows.card in /app/frontend/app/(consumer)/discover.tsx:839 (chipCard) and :874 (posterShadow). Non-blocking but should be migrated to boxShadow for RN 0.76+ / RN Web compatibility.

Console warns 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' — from /app/frontend/app/(consumer)/discover.tsx:611 where LinearGradient passes pointerEvents="none" as a prop instead of via style. Non-blocking. (Also reported in iteration_4.)

critical_code_review_comments: Icon swap is correctly applied at /app/frontend/app/(consumer)/discover.tsx:39-47 — every CATEGORIES entry now uses a filled Ionicons name with no transparent interior geometry: sparkles / musical-notes / color-palette / laptop / fast-food / trophy / apps. Choice of 'laptop' for Tech (instead of hardware-chip filled) is a good call — hardware-chip filled would still show a small centered die which could be misread as a box. 'fast-food' for Food and 'apps' for Other are visually distinct and readable at 30px.
Icon color still binds to `active ? accent : colors.onSurface` (:169), so filled shapes take the accent tint when selected — matches the halo/border colour and reads as one coherent chip.
Chip halo/elevation-on-outer-only workaround from iteration_4 (discover.tsx:174-187) is preserved, so the current filled-icon fix stacks on top of the earlier double-elevation fix cleanly.

activeCategory + headerTint memos (:588-600) still key off CATEGORIES[i].color, so the header wash automatically re-tints when a chip is tapped — verified visually across all 7 categories in both themes.

rca_of_issue: The 'white square' artifact reported by the user this iteration was not the Android elevation issue from iteration_3 — it was the outline Ionicons variants exposing their transparent interior negative space through the chip's semi-tinted background. musical-notes-outline has hollow note-heads, hardware-chip-outline has a hollow interior square (the die), color-palette-outline has a hollow thumb-hole, apps-outline is four hollow squares, etc. On an active chip (background = accent + '1A' at ~10% alpha over a colored halo), those transparent interiors read as bright shapes because the halo/lit area shows through them, giving the 'white/light box inside the icon' impression. Fix: swap every category icon in /app/frontend/app/(consumer)/discover.tsx:39-47 from *-outline to the filled variant, and for Tech pick 'laptop' (no interior geometry) instead of the filled hardware-chip which still has a centered die shape. Verified: all 14 states (7 cats x 2 themes) show clean, solid, opaque glyphs — no transparent interior artifact remains.
